_about: How the Asset Database's own data decides when a shared value (a phone number, a certificate, a name server, a fingerprint) is held by too many assets to be evidence about any one of them. For a kind of value, the histogram of how many holders each value has gives the median and spread of those counts in log scale; a value whose count's modified z-score is above k is a hub (Iglewicz and Hoaglin's usual cut is 3.5). A kind needs at least min_sample values before its counts decide; with fewer, the signal's fixed limit in signals.json applies. A derived limit is never below floor. A computed threshold is used for refresh_hours before it is computed again. options.hubs.derive set to false (or the lens -fixed-hubs flag) uses the fixed limits in signals.json throughout.
